transcript.text: Sometimes when I open the dishwasher there's grey smelly water in the bottom even though it finished draining fine. Not every day though. Kitchen sink was replaced last month if that matters.

The recent sink replacement does matter. The most likely explanation is dirty water backing up from the new sink waste into the dishwasher after it has successfully drained. That fits grey, smelly water which is intermittent rather than a dishwasher that simply cannot pump out. A partial blockage in the dishwasher filter/sump is the next possibility; less commonly, its non-return valve is allowing water back in. 1. Check the timing: after a normal dishwasher cycle, leave it empty and use the kitchen sink. Check the dishwasher bottom later. If water returns after sink use, this points strongly to the sink waste connection or drain-hose routing rather than the dishwasher pump. 2. With the dishwasher switched off and unplugged, look under the sink. The dishwasher drain hose should rise up as high as practicable beneath the worktop before it joins the sink waste, then drop to the connection. A low, sagging hose can let sink water run back. Also run the sink tap: it should drain freely, without backing up in the bowl. 3. Still switched off, remove and rinse the dishwasher filter, then clear visible food or greasy debris from the sump beneath it. Grey smelly water often comes from residue held there, and a partial restriction can make backflow worse. 4. At the sink-waste connection, check the hose is secure and the new waste fitting is not obstructed. If the sink drains poorly or the hose has no high loop, ask the sink fitter/plumber to correct that installation. If the water comes back even when the sink has not been used, despite a clean filter and a correctly routed hose, the dishwasher non-return valve or drain system needs investigating by an appliance engineer.

I checked a few of those. The water does seem to appear after I drain the sink full of washing-up water. Under the sink, the dishwasher hose just lies on the cupboard floor and goes straight into the waste spigot, so there's no high loop (it's been like that since the new sink went in). The filter was clean, and the sink drains a little slow. Should I raise the hose up?

Yes — the hose should be raised into a high loop, as high as practicable under the worktop, then secured there before it drops down to the sink-waste spigot. Its current route along the cupboard floor is very likely allowing the sink water to run back into the dishwasher. The slow sink drainage also needs sorting: a high loop reduces backflow, but a partially restricted trap or waste pipe can still force dirty water towards the dishwasher connection. As this began after the sink was replaced, the sink fitter/plumber should ideally correct both the hose routing and the slow-running waste. 1. With the dishwasher switched off and unplugged, raise the drain hose under the worktop and secure it with a proper clip/strap. Do not kink, crush or sharply bend it.
2. Have the sink trap and waste pipe cleared so the sink drains freely. Put towels down before any trap work, as it will contain dirty water.
3. Then empty the dishwasher, drain a sinkful of water, and check whether any water returns to the dishwasher. If it stays dry after the high loop and waste restriction are corrected, the dishwasher itself is fine. If water still returns despite that, the dishwasher non-return valve becomes the more likely cause and an appliance engineer should inspect it.

Ok, I looped the hose up high under the worktop and clipped it, then drained a sinkful of washing-up water. No more water in the dishwasher afterwards. Is that enough, or do I still need the slow sink looked at?

The slow sink is separate, but it is still worth having the trap/waste cleared if it remains noticeably slow. It will not necessarily make water return to the dishwasher now the hose is correctly looped, but slow drainage can lead to smells, sink backup and extra strain on the waste plumbing. Keep the hose clipped high and avoid kinks or it dropping back onto the cupboard floor. Is there anything else you would like to check?

candidates: Sink-waste connection or drain-hose arrangement allowing dirty sink water to run back into the dishwasher (high)
Partial blockage in the dishwasher filter, sump or drain path (medium)
